newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium starts small caps market with Ibt.
newsitem.headline: Belgium starts small caps market with Ibt.

text.p: Belgium's new growth stocks market, which is part of a four-country project to rival the Easdaq exchange, kicked into action on Friday with trading in cancer treatment firm International Brachytherapy (IBt).

IBt ended at the day's high of 980 francs, two percent under its share offer price of 1,000 and with 2,000 shares traded. The IPO of 250,000 shares, which ended in early March, had been slightly oversubscribed.
Brussels bourse deputy director Anne Vleminckx said this was a "more than honorable" start, adding the listing must be placed in context.
"(IBt) has potential, and it is also high risk. There is no production yet and it will be operational at best in 18 months," she added.

The firm plans to develop, make and sell radio therapeutic devices, called seeds, which can be implanted in a patient to treat prostate cancer in its early stages. The product will initially target the U.S. market.
The federation-style EURO.NM project involves interconnecting similar so-called "New Markets" in Paris, Frankfurt, Brussels and Amsterdam.
Trading began on the Paris new market, or Nouveau Marche, a year ago and Frankfurt's version opened last month.

Vleminckx said that under the EURO.NM's cross-membership project the Brussels market should be linked technically to the Paris market by the summer, to Amsterdam by the end of the year and to Frankfurt by next year.
The four will also share a common data feed.

EURO.NM faces a rival in Easdaq, a Brussels-based pan-European exchange for growth stocks, which currently has eight stocks listed. Easdaq began trading in November, and is a fledgling version of New York's successful Nasdaq exchange.
Easdaq says it will be distinguished from EURO.NM by its higher market capitalisation, now over one billion dollars, which boosted market liquidity.

Vleminckx said that while the profile of firms applying to the two markets could be the same, EURO.NM had the advantage of combining an order driven market - with twice daily fixings - and market making, while Easdaq only had market making.

"The order driven trading, where the price is determined by offer and demand, gives full price transparency. The advantage of market makers is it's better for liquidity," she said. EURO.NM also allowed comapnies to use their national accounting standards as well as international ones.
"Only the future will tell if there is room for both (Easdaq and EURO.NM)," she added, though noted there was an increased interest in risk capital among European investors.
Vleminckx expected between five and ten listings on the EURO.NM Belgium market within 12 months.
The bourse gave the green light for IBt's listing late last month after questioning the firm about legal claims against it.
